newsitem.title: USA: U.S. closes Brazzaville embassy, evacuates staff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. closes Brazzaville embassy, evacuates staff.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was temporarily closing its embassy in Brazzaville and would pull out its remaining embassy staff on Wednesday.

"We simply can't protect them any more given the deteriorating security situation," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters, saying there was "chaos and mayhem" in the city, which was gripped by a civil war.

Rebels and government troops have been fighting in the Congo Republic since June 5. Burns said the danger for U.S. personnel was increasing partly because French forces sent to evacuate civilians were pulling out.
"The State Department is suspending operations in Brazzaville as of ... Wednesday morning," Burns said.

"Our 12 official Americans -- our diplomats there -- a single Peace Corps volunteer who had remained in the country and a Peace Corps doctor will depart by a C130 from Brazzaville tomorrow," he told a regular news briefing.
He said a 12-member military team sent into the west African capital last week would leave at about the same time, carrying embassy equipment with them.
U.S. diplomats would establish a temporary listening post in Kinshasa, capital of the former Zaire across the Congo River from Brazzaville, to monitor developments.
Burns said U.S. diplomats had reported from Brazzaville that an international mediation committee had convinced the fighting forces on Tuesday to agree to a three-day truce.

"We'd like to see this truce implemented. We'd like to see the fighting stop completely," he said, complimenting the representatives of Gabon, France, Mali, Equatorial Guinea as well as the United States ambassador for helping bring it about.
He said Washington was not severing diplomatic relations with Congo and was not closing the embassy permanently. Local employees would look after the operations.
